text:
Consider a force $\vec{F}=-x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}$
. The work done
by this force in moving a particle from point
A(1, 0) to B(0, 1) along the line segment is :
(all quantities are in SI units)

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
W = $\int \vec{F}.d\vec{r}$

= $\int \left (-x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}\right ).\left (dx\hat{i}+dy\hat{j}\right )$

= $-\int\limits _{1}^{0}xdx+\int\limits _{0}^{1}ydy$

= $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}$ = 1 J

text:
A body A of mass m is moving in a circular orbit
of radius R about a planet. Another body B of
mass
$\frac{m}{2}$
collides with A with a velocity which is half $\left (\frac{\vec{v}}{2}\right )$ the instantaneous velocity$\vec{v}$
of A.
The collision is completely inelastic. Then, the
combined body :
options:
starts moving in an elliptical orbit around
the planet.

Falls vertically downwards towards the
planet
Escapes from the Planet's Gravitational field.
continues to move in a circular orbit
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Orbital speed for of A is v = $\sqrt{\frac{GM}{R}}$

After collision, let the combined mass moves
with speed $v_{1}$

$\therefore$ mv + $\frac{m}{2}\frac{v}{2}$ = $\left (\frac{3m}{2}\right )v_{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{1} =$ $\frac{5v}{6}$

Since after collision, the speed is not equal to
orbital speed at that point. So motion cannot be
circular. Since velocity will remain tangential,
so it cannot fall vertically towards the planet.
Their speed after collision is less than escape
speed $\sqrt{2}v$, so they cannot escape
gravitational field.
So their motion will be elliptical around the
planet.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
Consider a sphere of radius R which carries a
uniform charge density $ρ$. If a sphere of radius $\frac{R}{2}$ is carved out of it, as shown, the ratio $\frac{\left |E_{A}\leftarrow \right |}{\left |E_{B}\leftarrow \right |}$ of magnitude of electric field $E_{A}\leftarrow$ and $E_{B}\leftarrow$,
respectively, at points A and B due to the
remaining portion is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The remaining body is equivalent to the complete sphere (radius $R$, density $ρ$, centre O) together with a sphere of radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and density $-ρ$ at the cavity centre $O^{'}$. From the figure, A is the centre O of the big sphere and lies on the cavity surface, and B is on the outer surface on the far side, so $O^{'}A=\dfrac{R}{2}$ and $O^{'}B=\dfrac{R}{2}+R=\dfrac{3R}{2}$.

For a uniformly charged sphere of radius $r_{0}$, the field is $\dfrac{ρr}{3𝜖_{0}}$ at distance $r\leq r_{0}$ from its centre and $\dfrac{ρr_{0}^{3}}{3𝜖_{0}r^{2}}$ at $r\geq r_{0}$.

At A, the complete sphere gives zero (A is its centre) and the cavity sphere gives

$|⃗{E}_{A}|=\dfrac{ρ}{3𝜖_{0}}\cdot \dfrac{R}{2}=\dfrac{ρR}{6𝜖_{0}}$

At B, the two fields lie along the line $BOO^{'}$ in opposite directions:

$|⃗{E}_{B}|=\dfrac{ρR}{3𝜖_{0}}-\dfrac{ρ(R/2)^{3}}{3𝜖_{0}(3R/2)^{2}}=\dfrac{ρR}{3𝜖_{0}}-\dfrac{ρR}{54𝜖_{0}}=\dfrac{17ρR}{54𝜖_{0}}$

$\dfrac{|⃗{E}_{A}|}{|⃗{E}_{B}|}=\dfrac{ρR/6𝜖_{0}}{17ρR/54𝜖_{0}}=\dfrac{9}{17}=\dfrac{18}{34}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
The electric fields of two plane electromagnetic
plane waves in vacuum are given by

$E_{1}\leftarrow =E_{0}\hat{j}\cos (ωt-kx)$
and

$E_{2}\leftarrow =E_{0}\widehat{k}\cos (ωt-ky)$

At t = 0, a particle of charge q is at origin with

a velocity $\vec{v}=0.8c\hat{j}$ (c is the speed of light in
vacuum). The instantaneous force experienced
by the particle is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$⃗{E}_{1}=E_{0}\hat{j}\cos (ωt-kx)$ travels along $+\hat{i}$; since $\hat{j}\times \hat{k}=\hat{i}$, its magnetic field is $⃗{B}_{1}=\dfrac{E_{0}}{c}\hat{k}\cos (ωt-kx)$.

$⃗{E}_{2}=E_{0}\hat{k}\cos (ωt-ky)$ travels along $+\hat{j}$; since $\hat{k}\times \hat{i}=\hat{j}$, its magnetic field is $⃗{B}_{2}=\dfrac{E_{0}}{c}\hat{i}\cos (ωt-ky)$.

At $t=0$ at the origin every cosine equals 1, so $⃗{E}=E_{0}(\hat{j}+\hat{k})$ and $⃗{B}=\dfrac{E_{0}}{c}(\hat{i}+\hat{k})$.

$⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}=0.8c\hat{j}\times \dfrac{E_{0}}{c}(\hat{i}+\hat{k})=0.8E_{0}(-\hat{k}+\hat{i})$

$⃗{F}=q(⃗{E}+⃗{v}\times ⃗{B})=qE_{0}(\hat{j}+\hat{k}+0.8\hat{i}-0.8\hat{k})=E_{0}q(0.8\hat{i}+\hat{j}+0.2\hat{k})$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
A long, straight wire of radius a carries a current
distributed uniformly over its cross-section. The
ratio of the magnetic fields due to the wire at
distance
$\frac{a}{3}$
and 2$a$, respectively from the axis
of the wire is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Let current density be J.

$\therefore$ Applying Ampere's law. For point P

$\int \vec{B.}d\vec{l}=μ_{0}i$

$\Rightarrow$ $B_{P}2π\frac{a}{3}$ = $μ_{0}Jπ\frac{a^{2}}{9}$ ...(1)

$\therefore$ Applying Ampere's law. For point Q

$B_{Q}2π(2a)$ = $μ_{0}Jπa^{2}$ ...(2)

Dividing (1) by (2) we get

$\frac{B_{P}2π\frac{a}{3}}{B_{Q}4πa}=\frac{μ_{0}Jπ\frac{a2}{9}}{μ_{0}Jπa^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{B_{P}}{B_{Q}}=\frac{2}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

Consider two ideal diatomic gases A and B at
some temperature T. Molecules of the gas A are
rigid, and have a mass m. Molecules of the gas

have a mass $\frac{m}{4}$

Degree of freedom of a diatomic molecule if
vibration is present = 7

$\therefore$ $C_{V}^{A}$ = $\frac{5}{2}R$

and $C_{V}^{B}$ = $\frac{7}{2}R$

$\therefore$ $\frac{C_{V}^{A}}{C_{V}^{B}}=\frac{5}{7}$

text:
A particle moving with kinetic energy E has
de Broglie wavelength $λ$. If energy $\Delta$E is added

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

Also, $\frac{h}{\sqrt{2m(E+\Delta E)}}$ = $\frac{λ}{2}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{E+\Delta E}{E}=4$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$E = 3E

text:
Radiation, with wavelength 6561 $A^{o}$ falls on a
metal surface to produce photoelectrons. The
electrons are made to enter a uniform magnetic
field of $3 × 10^{–4} T$. If the radius of the largest
circular path followed by the electrons is
10 mm, the work function of the metal is
close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the work function be $𝜙$.

$\therefore$ $KE_{\max } =$ $\frac{hc}{λ}-𝜙$

We know r = $\frac{mv}{qB}$

and p = mv = rqB

$\therefore$ $KE_{\max } =$ $\frac{p^{2}}{2m}$ = $\frac{q^{2}r^{2}B^{2}}{2m}$

 = $\frac{\left (1.6\times 10^{-19}\right )^{2}\left (10\times 10^{-3}\right )^{2}\left (3\times 10^{-4}\right )^{2}}{2\times 9\times 10^{-31}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}}$

= 0.8 eV

$\frac{hc}{λ}$ = $\frac{12420}{6561}$ = 1.9 eV

$\therefore$ $𝜙$ = 1.9 - 0.8 = 1.1 eV

text:
Two particles of equal mass m have respective

initial velocities $u\hat{i}$ and $u\left (\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{2}\right )$.

They collide
completely inelastically. The energy lost in the
process is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{P_{i}}=P_{f}\leftarrow$

$\Rightarrow$ mu$\hat{i}$ + m$\left (\frac{u}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{u}{2}\hat{j}\right )$ = 2m$\vec{v}$

Compare both side

$\vec{v}=$ $\frac{3u}{4}\hat{i}+\frac{u}{4}\hat{j}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\vec{v}\right |^{2}$ = $\frac{10u^{2}}{16}$

$\DeltaKE = KE_{f} – KE_{i}$

= $\frac{1}{2}2m\times \frac{10u^{2}}{16}$ - $\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}$ - $\frac{1}{2}m\left (\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}$

= $-\frac{1}{8}mu^{2}$

text:
In the given circuit diagram, a wire is joining
points B and D. The current in this wire is :

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With B and D joined they form one node, so the $1\Omega$ and $4\Omega$ resistors are in parallel between A and B, and the $2\Omega$ and $3\Omega$ resistors are in parallel between B and C.

$R_{AB}=\dfrac{1\times 4}{1+4}=0.8\Omega ,R_{BC}=\dfrac{2\times 3}{2+3}=1.2\Omega$

$I=\dfrac{20}{0.8+1.2}=10\text{A}$

The current divides in inverse ratio of the resistances: the $1\Omega$ resistor carries $\dfrac{4}{5}\times 10=8\text{A}$ into B, and the $2\Omega$ resistor carries $\dfrac{3}{5}\times 10=6\text{A}$ out of B.

Junction rule at B: the wire BD carries $8-6=2\text{A}$, from B to D.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
A charged particle of mass 'm' and charge 'q'
moving under the influence of uniform electric
field $E\vec{i}$
and a uniform magnetic field $B\vec{k}$
follows a trajectory from point P to Q as shown
in figure. The velocities at P and Q are
respectively, $v\vec{i}$ and $-2v\vec{j}$
. Then which of the
following statements (A, B, C, D) are
correct ? 
(Trajectory shown is schematic and
not to scale) :

[IMG]


(A) E = $\frac{3}{4}\left (\frac{mv^{2}}{qa}\right )$

(B) Rate of work done by the electric field at P is $\frac{3}{4}\left (\frac{mv^{3}}{a}\right )$

(C) Rate of work done by both the fields at Q
is zero

(D) The difference between the magnitude of
angular momentum of the particle at P and
Q is 2mav.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the particle moving from point P to point Q,

$W_{$Electric field$} + W_{$Magnetic field} = $\Delta$KE

$\Rightarrow$ qE(2$a$) + 0 = $\frac{1}{2}m\left [(2v)^{2}-v^{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ 2qE$a$ = $\frac{3}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ E = $\frac{3}{4}\left (\frac{mv^{2}}{qa}\right )$

$\therefore$ Point (A) is correct.

Rate of work done(Power) by electric 

field at p = $\vec{F}.\vec{v}$ = qEv = $\frac{3}{4}\left (\frac{mv^{3}}{a}\right )$

$\therefore$ Point (B) is also correct.

Angle between electric force and velocity is
90º, hence rate of work done will be zero at Q.

$\therefore$ Point (C) is also correct.

Initial angular momentum at P, $\vec{L}_{i}$ = mv$a\left (-\widehat{k}\right )$

Final angular momentum at Q, $\vec{L}_{f}$ = m(2v)$(2a)\left (-\widehat{k}\right )$

Change in angular momentum $\vec{L}_{f}$ – $\vec{L}_{i}$ = $3mva\left (-\widehat{k}\right )$

Magnitude in the change in angular momentum $\left |\Delta \vec{L}\right |$ = $3mva$

$\therefore$ Point (D) is wrong.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
Three harmonic waves having equal frequency
$ν$ and same intensity $I_{0}$, have phase angles 0, $\frac{π}{4}$ and $-\frac{π}{4}$ respectively. When they are
superimposed the intensity of the resultant wave
is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equal intensities mean equal amplitudes $A$, with $I_{0}=kA^{2}$.

The phasors at phase $+\dfrac{π}{4}$ and $-\dfrac{π}{4}$ are symmetric about the phase-0 phasor: their perpendicular components cancel and their components along it add to $2A\cos \dfrac{π}{4}=\sqrt{2}A$.

$A_{R}=A+\sqrt{2}A=(1+\sqrt{2})A$

$I_{R}=kA_{R}^{2}=(1+\sqrt{2})^{2}kA^{2}=(3+2\sqrt{2})I_{0}\approx 5.8I_{0}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
Water flows in a horizontal tube (see figure).

The pressure of water changes by $700 Nm^{–2}$

between A and B where the area of cross section

are $40 cm^{2}$ and $20 cm^{2}$, respectively. Find the

rate of flow of water through the tube.

(density of water = 1000 kgm$^{–3})$

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Rate of flow of water is same at both A and B

$A_{A}V_{A} = A_{B}V_{B}$

$(40)V_{A} = (20)V_{B}$

$V_{B} = 2V_{A} .......(1)$

Using Bernoulli's theorem

$P_{A} +$ $\frac{1}{2}ρV_{A}^{2}$ $= P_{B} +$ $\frac{1}{2}ρV_{B}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $P_{A} - P_{B} =$ $\frac{1}{2}ρV_{B}^{2}$ - $\frac{1}{2}ρV_{A}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 700 = $\frac{1}{2}\times 1000\left (4V_{A}^{2}-V_{A}^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $V_{A} = 0.68 m/s = 68 cm/s$

$\therefore$ Flow rate $= A_{A}V_{A} = (40)(68) = 2720 cm^{3}/s$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
One end of a straight uniform 1m long bar is
pivoted on horizontal table. It is released from
rest when it makes an angle 30º from the
horizontal (see figure). Its angular speed when
it hits the table is given as $\sqrt{n}$ $s^{-1}$, where n is
an integer. The value of n is $_________$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By energy conservation

$U_{i} + K_{i} = U_{f} + K_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $mg\frac{l}{2}\sin 30^{\circ }$ + 0 = 0 + $\frac{1}{2}Iω^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $mg\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{1}{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{m(1)^{2}}{3}ω^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω^{2}=\frac{3g}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω=\sqrt{15}$

$\therefore$ n = 15

text:
The distance x covered by a particle in one
dimensional motion varies with time t as

$x^{2} =$ at$^{2} + 2bt + c$. If the acceleration of the
particle depends on x as $x^{–n}$, where n is an
integer, the value of n is $__________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $x^{2}=at^{2}+2bt+c$. Differentiating with respect to $t$, with $v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}$:

$2xv=2at+2b\Rightarrow xv=at+b\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{at+b}{x}$

Differentiating $xv=at+b$ again, with acceleration $A=\dfrac{dv}{dt}$:

$v^{2}+xA=a\Rightarrow A=\dfrac{a-v^{2}}{x}=\dfrac{ax^{2}-(at+b)^{2}}{x^{3}}$

Substituting $x^{2}=at^{2}+2bt+c$ in the numerator:

$ax^{2}-(at+b)^{2}=a^{2}t^{2}+2abt+ac-a^{2}t^{2}-2abt-b^{2}=ac-b^{2}$

So $A=\dfrac{ac-b^{2}}{x^{3}}\propto x^{-3}$, which gives $n=3$.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
A body of mass m = 10 kg is attached to one
end of a wire of length 0.3 m. The maximum
angular speed (in rad $s^{–1})$ with which it can be
rotated about its other end in space station is :

(Breaking stress of wire $= 4.8 × 10^{7} Nm^{–2}$ and

area of cross-section of the wire $= 10^{–2} cm^{2})$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
T = m$ω^{2}l$

Breaking stress = $σ$ = $\frac{mω^{2}l}{A}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω^{2}$ = $\frac{4.8\times 10^{7}\times \left (10^{-2}\times 10^{-4}\right )}{10\times 0.3}$ = 16

$\Rightarrow$ $ω$ = 4

text:
Both the diodes used in the circuit shown are
assumed to be ideal and have negligible
resistance when these are forward biased. Built
in potential in each diode is 0.7 V. For the input
voltages shown in the figure, the voltage
(in Volts) at point A is $__________$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Both diodes have their cathodes at A, which is connected to ground through the resistor; the left diode has its anode at 12.7 V and the right diode has its anode at 4 V.

The left diode, with the higher anode voltage, conducts. With a built-in potential of 0.7 V and negligible forward resistance it fixes

$V_{A}=12.7-0.7=12\text{V}$

The right diode then has 4 V on its anode and 12 V on its cathode, so it is reverse biased and carries no current.

Hence, the answer is 12.
